subject: Qualification + PoC plan — deployment mode options (Hosted vs Dedicated)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <s.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification + PoC plan — deployment mode options (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on deployment mode requirements and a short PoC/ trial plan.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: validate inference quality and unit economics for your customer-facing assistant.
- Deployment constraints: data residency / contractual SLA needs; ability to isolate workloads (finance/legal data).
- Initial preference: evaluate both Hosted API (fast to start) and Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + isolation) to compare latency/cost. Private VPC/on-prem likely later if regulatory gate requires it.

Proposed 4-week PoC plan (low-effort, side-by-side):
Week 1 — Hosted evaluation: baseline integration with Hosted API using sample traffic (sanitized).
Week 2 — Dedicated trial: provision temporary dedicated capacity with same model/config for throughput & latency testing.
Week 3 — Workload validation: run production-like traffic, measure p95 latency, concurrency behavior, KV/prefix cache hit rates.
Week 4 — Wrap + decision: present results and recommended deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated) and next steps to procurement/security.

Success criteria (examples — please confirm):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for single-turn generation at our typical payload size
- Throughput: sustain 500 req/min with <5% error rate under burst
- Quality: automated eval pass rate >= 90% on your benchmark prompts
- Cost thumb rule: projected cost per 1M tokens < $X (we'll provide model-by-model estimate)

Attachments: I attached a short PoC plan and our SOC2 summary.

Can you confirm: 1) the stakeholders we should loop in on the PoC (infra, security, procurement), 2) any non-negotiable technical constraints (VPC-only traffic, IP allowlist), and 3) target timeline for kickoff?

If this looks good I can schedule the kickoff and get a temporary dedicated pool ready to spin up.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Acme_PoC_plan.pdf
Attachment: SOC2-Summary.pdf

From: Samantha Li <s.li@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Gomez <c.gomez@acmecorp.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification + PoC plan — deployment mode options (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Ben — helpful summary.

We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity for the PoC because:
- Data residency: finance data needs to remain in our US region and isolated from general multitenant pools.
- SLA & performance predictability: we need consistent p95 latency targets for a demo with partners.

Stakeholders to include:
- Carlos Gomez (Dir, Infrastructure) — will own provisioning/whitelisting
- Anita Shah (Head of Product) — will validate quality/UX
- I'll loop Procurement once we have a rough cost/term estimate

Timeline: May pilot start preferred (we have an internal launch in June). Can you provide a rough cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for the expected traffic profile? Also attaching our internal security questionnaire — Carlos will review.

On non-negotiables: IP allowlist and a DPA are musts. We can run data through Hosted for initial quality checks only if we can ensure token-level encryption in transit and no long-term retention.

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
s.li@acmecorp.com

Attachment: Acme_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <s.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification + PoC plan — deployment mode options (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Great — thanks for the quick response, Samantha.

We can do Dedicated as the primary PoC track and keep Hosted as a quick baseline step (sanitized traffic only, as you suggested). Quick answers:
- Cost delta: I'll send a model-by-model estimate by EOD Monday; rough ballpark: Dedicated has an up-front provisioning cost but reduces per-token unit cost at scale (will quantify).
- IP allowlist & DPA: noted — Marissa from Security is CC'd and will own the DPA / compliance side.

Proposed updated milestones (Dedicated-first):
1) Pre-kickoff (this week): exchange network allowlist, sample payload, and finalize metrics.
2) Week 1 (setup): provision dedicated pool (temp creds), smoke tests, basic integration.
3) Week 2 (scale tests): run ramp tests for throughput and latency under production-like load.
4) Week 3 (quality evaluation): run benchmark prompts and human review with Anita + Product.
5) Week 4 (review): present results, cost estimate, and recommended deployment.

Success criteria (finalized with your team):
- p95 < 200ms under steady-state load
- Error rate < 5% during bursts to 1.5x expected QPS
- Product acceptance meeting: Anita signs off on quality for the key user flows

I'll upload the detailed cost estimate and a PoC runbook (with test harness notes) to the Drive link and share with you Monday. Can we aim to kick off the week of May 3?

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Samantha / Ben —

Quick security/compliance note from my side. We can support a Dedicated trial while we finalize the DPA. Attached is our SOC2 summary and a draft DPA for review. A few operational asks so the Dedicated pool can be provisioned quickly:
- IP allowlist for any outbound admin or collector endpoints (please provide CIDR ranges)
- Confirmation of required retention policy (we default to ephemeral log retention for PoC unless otherwise requested)
- NDA/Procurement: we can operate under a short-term MSA/PO for the pilot; Procurement will want term/credit info before production.

I can review Acme's security questionnaire (thanks for sending) and will follow up with specifics by Monday. If helpful I can schedule a 30-min sync with Carlos next week to go over network/ops.

Looping in a short technical kickoff checklist so Carlos/ops can see what we need from them to stand up the Dedicated trial. Quoting Ben's original plan below for context.

On Thu, 25 Mar 2027 at 14:12 Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed 4-week PoC plan (low-effort, side-by-side):
> Week 1 — Hosted evaluation: baseline integration with Hosted API using sample traffic (sanitized).
> Week 2 — Dedicated trial: provision temporary dedicated capacity with same model/config for throughput & latency testing.
> Week 3 — Workload validation: run production-like traffic, measure p95 latency, concurrency behavior, KV/prefix cache hit rates.
> Week 4 — Wrap + decision: present results and recommended deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated) and next steps to procurement/security.

Technical kickoff checklist:
- Admin access: list of admin emails for Redwood provisioning and a contact person for Acme ops (Carlos?)
- Network: CIDR ranges and any proxy details (we support static egress IPs or VPC peering for Dedicated)
- Sample payload: 1000 sanitized requests and a representative prompt set
- Expected QPS/burst profile: baseline QPS and expected peak bursts
- Preferred model(s) to test (we can suggest tuned variants)

If you can share the sample payload and a target date for the week of May 3 we will reserve capacity and send over temp creds for the Dedicated pool.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
